text:
Rasmus Andersson came to Vegas from Calgary with a reputation as a big-minute, puck-moving right shot, and the first full season has been hard. Daily Hive's headline earlier this month said he is "continuing to struggle with Golden Knights," and the stat line agrees: three goals and seven points in 26 games, none of them on the power play.

Our numbers say a good part of it is bad luck. Vegas has scored 13 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and his own shooting is right where it should be at 6.2%. That is the kind of hole that usually fills back in, so we mark him due.

Not all of it is luck, though. The Golden Knights get 47% of the 5v5 shot attempts and 49% of the expected goals with him out there, and both are about five points worse than when he sits. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 34th among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense. The points should follow the chances; the 5v5 share is what needs fixing.
headline: Rasmus Andersson, stuck in a rough patch
